title: Annotheca
description: A reference manager built for research with AI assistants: through MCP, Claude files the papers it cites with metadata verified at the source, so its bibliography cannot contain hallucinated references.
detail:
Language models are good at finding papers and bad at citing them: a swapped author, a wrong year, a title that does not exist. Annotheca removes that risk. It runs an MCP server, so Claude, or any assistant that speaks MCP, never writes a reference itself: it only says which paper it means, by DOI, arXiv ID or citation, and Annotheca resolves the metadata from doi.org, arXiv and Crossref and returns the exact citation key, title and authors to use.

Every paper an assistant adds is marked with its name and comes with a note on why it matters, so the bibliography an AI relied on can always be traced and checked. The assistant can also read my notes and highlights before summarising a paper, and get the project's .bib file to cite with LaTeX. A single command, annotheca connect, plugs it into Claude Code and Claude Desktop.

Underneath is the reference manager I needed for my own research: one place per project, organised by stage (state of the art, method, experiments), with open-access PDFs downloaded automatically, highlights, sticky notes and one clean .bib per project. A paper filed in two folders is stored once but annotated separately in each, and a whole project can be shared as a single file.

Open source and published on PyPI: pip install annotheca.
